entry.title: The Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL phones are $250 off
entry.summary: During Amazon’s October sale, the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL are discounted by $250 or more. The base model Pixel 11 Pro with 256GB of storage is only $849 (originally $1,099), $50 lower than the usual price for the base Pixel 11, while the 256GB 11 Pro XL is $999, a $300 […]
entry.content:
During Amazon’s October sale, the Pixel 11 Pro and Pixel 11 Pro XL are discounted by $250 or more. The base model Pixel 11 Pro with 256GB of storage is only $849 (originally $1,099), $50 lower than the usual price for the base Pixel 11, while the 256GB 11 Pro XL is $999, a $300 price break.

Even the regular Pixel 11 with 256GB of storage is cheaper, selling at $749, $150 off the normal price. But with the Pro at just a $100 premium over the Pixel 11 right now instead of $200, its superior cameras alone is a pretty convincing reason to spend more.

Google Pixel 11 Pro

Where to Buy:

  • $1099 $849 at Amazon
  • $1099 $899 at Google
  • $1099 $849 at Best Buy

We praised the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL for their new camera modes, as well as the Magic Capture mode. We liked some of the Gemini-assisted features, like Rambler for smoothing out voice texting, but others, like proactive assistance, felt a bit more narrow.

Read our Pixel 11 Pro review and our Pixel 11 review.

entry.content:
Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days event has begun, and it lasts through 3AM ET on Thursday, October 8th. We’ve spun through the company’s huge list of deals to find products that Verge readers will like (and that we personally like, too). There are plenty of headphone deals, plus some great products in the home entertainment space. Also, the discounts are spectacular on Pixel 11 phones, the A17 Pro-equipped iPad Mini, and the M5 MacBook Air.

We’re changing up how we’re presenting the deals. Usually, these posts are huge and require a lot of scrolling, but we wanted to make it easier to find what you’re looking for. All of the deals are in a table that you can sort by category.

We’ll add more deals as we find them, and we’ll also include links to various category-specific roundups we’ll be publishing throughout the sale.

.duet--layout--rail { pointer-events: none; } .duet--layout--rail div { pointer-events: auto; }

iPhone Air

The iPhone Air is Apple’s thinnest iPhone yet at 5.6mm, featuring a 6.5-inch ProMotion display, a 48MP fusion camera, and an 18MP front camera with Center Stage support. But its single rear camera and “meh” battery life mean it’s not for everyone.

Where to Buy:

  • $999.99 $839.99 at Best Buy (256GB)

iPhone 16E

The iPhone 16E is the spiritual successor to the iPhone SE, bringing flagship-level performance for less than the standard 16. We really wish it included MagSafe for $599, but those upgrading from older iPhones will probably be satisfied with what’s included.

Where to Buy:

  • $599.99 $489.99 at Best Buy (128GB)

Belkin Charging Case Pro

While it won’t charge your Switch 2 any faster than the cheaper Belkin option, the clever battery-meets-kickstand with a built-in display simply looks better.

Where to Buy:

  • $99.99 $80.74 at Amazon (sand)
  • $99.99 $84.99 at Belkin (sand)

Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

Samsung recently increased the price of all its S26 phones, but you can get the best of the bunch, the S26 Ultra, at one of its best prices of the year. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $1299.99 $979.99 at Amazon (256GB)
  • $1299.99 $1099.99 at Best Buy (256GB)
  • $1499.99 $1179.99 at Amazon (512GB)

Bose QuietComfort Headphones Gen 2

If all you want is great sound, strong noise cancellation, and physical buttons to navigate, you can’t do better than the Bose QC headphones at this price. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $359 $169 at Amazon
  • $359 $319 at Best Buy
  • $359 at Bose

Anker Laptop Power Bank

Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.

Where to Buy:

  • $119.99 $95.99 at Amazon
  • $119.99 $95.99 at Best Buy
  • $119.99 $95.99 at Anker

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8

The passport-style Z Fold 8 is the closest thing to an iPhone Duo on the Android side, at least in the US. It’s an awesome phone at its biggest discount to date. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $1899.99 $1549.99 at Amazon
  • $1899.99 $1649.99 at Best Buy

Soundcore Liberty 5 Pro

If you like to yap on the phone, these earbuds yield the best call quality of any we’ve tried (it’s not even close), and they sound great for music, too. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $169.99 $135.99 at Amazon
  • $169.99 $135.99 at Anker

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra

While not as head-turning of a foldable as Samsung’s Z Fold 8, the Ultra delivers better camera quality. It’s cheaper than ever right now. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $2099.99 $1699.99 at Amazon
  • $2099.99 $1849.99 at Best Buy

Roku Ultra

Roku’s latest Ultra streamer has built-in ethernet, a rechargeable voice remote with backlit buttons, and AirPlay 2 support. You can also control it with Amazon Alexa through a compatible smart speaker. The Roku Channel app lets you stream over 400 free live TV stations, plus exclusive movies like Weird: The Al Yankovic Story.

Where to Buy:

  • $149.99 $99.99 at Amazon
  • $149.99 $99.99 at Best Buy
  • $149.99 $99.99 at B&H Photo

Roku Streaming Stick Plus

Roku’s Streaming Stick Plus supports 4K playback and features a slim design, so it won’t block nearby ports. It plugs straight into your TV’s HDMI port and can be powered by your TV’s USB port, so you don’t need an additional plug. It also comes with Roku’s Voice Remote, giving you hands-free control.

Where to Buy:

  • $59.99 $34.99 at Amazon
  • $59.99 $34.99 at Walmart
  • $59.99 $34.99 at Best Buy

WiiM Mini

The WiiM Mini makes it easy to wirelessly stream music from your phone, a streaming service, or other local storage to existing speakers you already have. It supports AirPlay 2 and a variety of streaming services.

Where to Buy:

  • $125 $84.15 at Amazon
  • $125 $84.15 at Crutchfield

Sonos Sub 4

The Sub 4, while not cheap, is the best sub for your Sonos setup. It can sit upright, or you can lay it down to fit under a couch or entertainment system.

Where to Buy:

  • $899 $749 at Amazon
  • $899 $749 at Sonos
  • $899 $749 at Best Buy

Sonos Beam (second-gen)

The latest Sonos Beam is a compact soundbar that supports a virtual Dolby Atmos effect and can stream music from a plethora of services. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $499 $359 at Amazon
  • $499 $359 at Sonos
  • $499 $299 at Sonos (refurbished)

SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni

The Omni delivers small, but welcome improvements over the 2022 Nova Pro, most notably a true platform-agnostic design that works with all consoles. Read our hands-on.

Where to Buy:

  • $399.99 $359.99 at Amazon
  • $399.99 $359.99 at Best Buy

Samsung Galaxy S26

While the S26 isn’t particularly impressive in any way, it’s one of the most affordable (yet most powerful) flagship phones you can currently get. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $899.99 $724.99 at Amazon (256GB)
  • $899.99 $799.99 at Best Buy (256GB)
  • $1099.99 $899.99 at Amazon (512GB)

Google Pixel 11

The Pixel 11 recently debuted at $899, but it recently got a whopping $150 price cut for the 256GB version. It’s the cheapest way to try Google’s new software features. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $899 $749 at Amazon

  • $899 $749 at Best Buy

If you value better picture quality and trust that Google might improve on the HiLight LED feature, the Pixel 11 Pro is the one to get, and it got a big discount for Prime Day. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $1099 $849 at Amazon
  • $1099 $899 at Google
  • $1099 $849 at Best Buy

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL

Google’s biggest Pixel 11 Pro got a sizeable price cut, too, making it $300 cheaper than the base iPhone 18 Pro Max model.

Where to Buy:

  • $1299 $999 at Amazon
  • $1299 $1049 at Google
  • $1299 $999 at Best Buy

Bose QuietComfort Ultra headphones (second-gen)

The best wireless headphones that Bose makes are discounted, and the company recently made them even better. Read our latest coverage.

Where to Buy:

  • $449 $369 at Amazon
  • $449 $369 at Walmart
  • $449 $369 at Best Buy

WiiM Amp

Enjoy a big discount on the WiiM Amp, which supports AirPlay 2, as well as several other wireless options. It also hosts a bunch of ports, allowing for passive stereo output, plus optical audio, HDMI ARC, and more. Read our coverage.

Where to Buy:

Apple AirPods Max (second-gen)

Apple’s new iteration of its priciest, most powerful headphones deliver minor updates for first-gen owners. But those who are jumping in will especially appreciate their big, bold sound. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $549 at Apple

  • $1199.99 $899.99 at Best Buy (65-inch)

Where to Buy:

  • $629.99 $479.99 at Best Buy (32GB)

Where to Buy:

  • $499.99 $379.99 at Best Buy

  • $249.99 $189.99 at Best Buy
  • $249.99 at Target

A new version of the Fit Pro wireless earbuds, which are upgraded with a redesigned wing tip that Beats says is 20 percent more flexible, a smaller case, and other advantages.

Beats Powerbeats Pro 2

  • $249.99 $179.99 at Best Buy

Beats Studio Pro

Despite the familiar design, there were plenty of upgrades in the latest Studio Pro, including noise cancellation, transparency mode, and lossless USB-C audio. Here’s our review.

  • $349.99 $119.95 at Amazon
  • $349.99 $119.95 at Walmart
  • $349.99 $149.99 at Best Buy

Apple 13-inch MacBook Air (M5)

Powered by Apple’s new M5 chip, the latest MacBook Airs are more powerful than prior models and offer double the base storage (512GB). They also support faster wireless standards, specifically Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $1299 $1099 at Amazon
  • $1299 $1099 at Best Buy

Apple MacBook Air (15-inch, M5, 2026)

For a slightly bigger MacBook Air, the 15-inch version is the one to get. It offers similar performance, but its battery is larger, and it has more speakers.

Where to Buy:

  • $1499 $1299 at Amazon
  • $1499 $1299 at Best Buy

iPad Mini (2024)

The seventh-gen iPad Mini comes with Apple’s A17 Pro chip and support for Apple Intelligence. It’s also compatible with the Apple Pencil Pro and offers faster Wi-Fi and USB-C speeds. Read our review.

  • $599 $499 at Amazon (128GB, Wi-Fi)
  • $599 $449 at Best Buy (128GB, Wi-Fi)
  • $699 $599 at Amazon (256GB, Wi-Fi)

Bose SoundLink Max

Bose’s SoundLink Max improves on the smaller Flex with true stereo sound — and very powerful sound at that. It’s got a removable handle for easy transport, and there’s an aux input for playing audio when you want to listen at a higher quality than what Bluetooth can deliver. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $399 $279 at Amazon
  • $399 $279 at Best Buy
  • $399 $279 at Bose

Bose SoundLink Plus

For something between Bose’s SoundLink Flex and the Max, the Plus strikes a good balance with booming bass, loud volume that doesn’t get distorted, and an easy-to-clean design. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $269 $179 at Amazon
  • $269 $179 at Best Buy
  • $269 $179 at Bose

Bose Soundlink Flex (second-gen)

The second-gen SoundLink Flex builds on the original with more intuitive controls, including a new play / pause button. It also adds adjustable EQ and support for higher-quality audio via AAC and aptX, while retaining a rugged IP67-rated design and the ability to pair two speakers for stereo sound.

Where to Buy:

  • $159 $119 at Amazon
  • $159 $119 at Walmart
  • $159 $119 at Best Buy

Belkin Charging Case for Nintendo Switch 2

The case features an integrated power bank and a small pocket to stow an AirTag (or other similarly sized Bluetooth tracker).

Where to Buy:

  • $69.99 $56.61 at Amazon (in black or sand)
  • $69.99 $59.49 at Best Buy
  • $69.99 $59.49 at Belkin

Belkin MagSafe 15W 2-in-1 wireless charging dock

A slick 2-in-1 charger that can charge your magnet-friendly iPhone or Pixel at a relatively speedy pace. Its extra charging pad supports AirPods, the Apple Watch, and other Qi-ready accessories.

Where to Buy:

  • $120 $59.99 at Amazon

Asus ProArt 27-inch 1440p USB-C monitor

An affordable color-accurate monitor that can easily connect to a MacBook or Windows machine that has USB-C video support. It’s a good price for a fully-featured 1440p monitor.

Where to Buy:

  • $299 $249 at Amazon

Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 foldable charging dock

Slap a recent iPhone onto this charging pad and it’ll charge at fast 25W speeds. It can also charge AirPods, and includes a cord and wall adapter.

Where to Buy:

  • $60 $42.99 at Amazon
  • $100 $75 at Amazon (w/ Apple Watch support)

Xreal xbx A01 Plus

Xreal’s most affordable set of USB-C display glasses yet. They lack three degrees of freedom, but are otherwise an awesome value for gaming or watching movies with your own huge, private screen. Read our hands-on.

Where to Buy:

  • $299.99 at Best Buy
  • $299.99 $254 at Xreal

Nothing Ear 3A earbuds

The Ear 3A are fantastic (and visually-striking) wireless earbuds for iPhone or Android selling at their best-ever price. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $99 $79 at Amazon
  • $99 $79 at Walmart
  • $99 $79 at Nothing

Eufy FamiLock S3 Max

Get you a smart lock that has a digital peephole, and that can be unlocked with a wave. This is a nice discount off its original $400 price. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $399.99 $279.99 at Amazon
  • $399.99 $319.99 at Best Buy
  • $399.99 $279.99 at Eufy

Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.

Where to Buy:

  • $999.99 $699.99 at Best Buy
  • $999.99 $699.99 at Roborock

Roborock Saros 20

Roborock’s Saros 20 stands out for its ability to climb tall thresholds, avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy, and clean under low furniture thanks to its slim design. It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms.

Where to Buy:

  • $1599.99 $1179.99 at Amazon
  • $1599.99 $1194.99 at Roborock

Aqara Smart Lock U400

This innovative new smart lock uses the U1 ultra-wideband (UWB) chip in many iPhones and Apple Watches to automatically unlock your door as you approach. It will also work with the new Aliro standard and be compatible with Android phones for hands-free unlocking.

Where to Buy:

  • $269.99 $219.99 at Amazon
  • $269.99 at Aqara

Aqara Doorbell Camera G400 with chime

The G400 was the first wired-only video doorbell to work with Apple’s HomeKit Secure Video feature. It has solid specs for the price, and includes a chime to sound indoors.

Where to Buy:

  • $99.99 $84.99 at Amazon

Hatch Restore 3

The Restore 3 features more than 50 sleep sounds and 18 adjustable light colors, with access to hundreds more through the optional Hatch Plus subscription, which runs $4.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

Where to Buy:

Kodak Charmera Keychain Digital Camera

Described by our writer Andrew Liszewski as “terrible,” the Charmera is still worth getting if you want a keychain camera that’s a ton of fun to use. Read our coverage.

Where to Buy:

  • $34.99 $29.74 at Amazon

LifeStraw personal water filter

LifeStraw’s basic filter removes unwanted bacteria and microplastics as you drink, giving you a safe way to hydrate no matter where you are.

Where to Buy:

  • $17.95 $12.98 at Amazon
  • $17.95 at Walmart
  • $17.95 at Lifestraw

TP-Link Tapo Matter-Certified Smart Plug Mini

A smart plug adds functionality to an existing gadget rather than replacing it. Once the plug is connected to your Wi-Fi network and a gadget, you can turn it on and off using an app. TP-Link’s Tapo smart plug supports Matter, so you can add it to whichever smart home platform you use. 

Where to Buy:

  • $19.99 $7.99 at Amazon

TP-Link Tapo 2K Outdoor pan/tilt wired floodlight camera

A semi-affordable (subscription-free) outdoor security camera that supplies both a floodlight and a pan/tilt design so that you can easily track visitors.

Where to Buy:

  • $99.99 $69.99 at Amazon

Ugreen two-bay DH2300 NAS

If you’re itching to locally host photos, files, videos, and more instead of paying for cloud storage, this entry-level NAS from Ugreen is discounted. You’ll just need to pack it with NAS-ready HDDs.

Where to Buy:

  • $269.99 $204.99 at Amazon

Apple Watch SE 3

The Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $249 $199 at Amazon

AirPods Pro 3

The AirPods Pro 3 have a new design that improves their fit, superior noise cancellation, better bass, and fairly accurate heart rate sensors. Read our review.

Where to Buy:

  • $249 $179 at Amazon
  • $249 $179 at Walmart
  • $249 $179 at Best Buy

Anker UFO 3-in-1 Qi2 15W charging dock

While not the fastest wireless charger at this price, Anker’s unique, UFO-styled 3-in-1 charging puck unfolds with pads for a phone, AirPods, and an Apple Watch.

Where to Buy:

  • $89.99 $59.99 at Amazon

Anker Nano 100W universal travel adapter

Anker’s powerful Nano international travel charger is great if you have a lot of USB-C gadgets to keep charged. While it lacks an AC plug, it supplies a screen that shows how much power you’re pushing to each port.

Where to Buy:

  • $79.99 $63.99 at Amazon

Anker Nano 45W charger with display

Anker’s latest single-port USB-C charger offers up to 45W of power, foldable prongs, and a front-facing “smart display” that lets you see the charge level, power flow, and other useful information at a glance.

Where to Buy:

  • $39.99 $23.99 at Amazon
  • $39.99 $25.99 at Anker

Philips Hue Festavia string lights

These smart lights have beautiful colors, a nice selection of festive scenes, and an easy-to-use app. They are super reliable when paired with a Hue Bridge and also work over Bluetooth. They come in three lengths, work with all the major smart home platforms, and are Matter-compatible.

Where to Buy:

  • $259.99 $186.99 at Amazon (65-foot)
  • $395.99 $305.97 at Amazon (130-foot)
  • $259.99 at Philips Hue (65-foot)

Philips Hue Essential four-pack of bulbs

Philips Hue bulbs can be pricey, which is why the company’s four-pack of Essential A19 bulbs are a great buy. They’re cheaper, costing less now during Prime Day than usual. They have adjustable colors, brightness, and can be controlled with Bluetooth or with a Hue Bridge (sold separately).

Where to Buy:

  • $59.99 $44.97 at Amazon (four-pack)

Bissell ProHeat 2X Revolution Pet Pro Plus carpet cleaner

Bissell’s Little Green is handy, but doesn’t cut it for big jobs. If you have pets and a lot of carpet to clean, this is one of the most powerful upright carpet cleaners in its price range.

Where to Buy:

  • $279.99 $209.99 at Amazon
  • $279.99 $237.99 at Best Buy
  • $279.99 $209.99 at Bissell

Govee Lightwall

It’s a Lightwall. What more do you need to know? Fine, it’s a curtain of lights that’s 8.5 feet wide and 6.2 feet tall with 1,536 LEDs. You can program them to show anything you want.

Where to Buy:

  • $449.99 $369.99 at Amazon
  • $449.99 $369.99 at Govee

Govee outdoor lamp post light

The outdoor lamp post light boasts full support for Google Assistant, Alexa, and Matter, so you can easily incorporate the lights into your smart home setup. 

Where to Buy:

  • $259.99 $149.99 at Amazon (at checkout)
  • $259.99 $159.99 at Govee

Govee Table Lamp 2

The color-changing Govee Table Lamp 2 is an especially great pick for grads looking to make a new space feel like home. With adjustable warmth and brightness, plus lights that sync to music, it’s easy to set the mood for relaxing, focusing, or partying. It can also be controlled with voice assistants or a simple tap for added convenience.

Where to Buy:

  • $79.99 $53.99 at Amazon
  • $79.99 $69.99 at Best Buy
  • $79.99 $53.99 at Target

Baseus AM52 power bank (with built-in cable)

This 10,000mAh power bank is one of the best ones available at this price. It has a built-in USB-C cable, and it’s MagSafe-ready, supporting up to 25W wireless charging speed for recent iPhones. Read our coverage.

The Blood of Dawnwalker

A new third-person adventure game made by several developers responsible for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. Dawnwalker is similar in terms of its branching storyline and great side quests, but unique with how vampirism affects gameplay.

Where to Buy:

Elgato Key Light

A 2800-lumen light that can illuminate your desk area for video meetings, close work, and other uses. It includes a desk clamp to make it easy to fix to your working surface.

Where to Buy:

entry.title: Reverse-engineered games: All the news on video game decomps, recomps, VR and web and 3D ports
entry.summary: It’s a wild time for retro gaming. Thanks to decompilations and recompilations of classic titles, those games are becoming unshackled from their proprietary code and original hardware to be ported to new devices or updated in ways to completely change the original game. Ever imagined skateboarding in Call of Duty? Or playing the original Halo right […]
entry.content:
It’s a wild time for retro gaming. Thanks to decompilations and recompilations of classic titles, those games are becoming unshackled from their proprietary code and original hardware to be ported to new devices or updated in ways to completely change the original game. Ever imagined skateboarding in Call of Duty? Or playing the original Halo right in your web browser, complete with multiplayer?  

These are unofficial versions of games, so they may sit in a legal gray area. It seems unlikely that Nintendo, for example, is particularly happy about people finding ways to play The Legend of Zelda on non-Nintendo hardware. Many of these projects are also made with the assistance of AI, which, for some people, is a non-starter given ethical or environmental concerns surrounding the technology.

Below, you’ll find our coverage of gaming decomps, recomps, and all the other ways gamers are reverse-engineering games to go previously unimaginable places.

  • Just think: You could be playing Halo in a web browser right now.
  • This unofficial Lego Racers remake runs in your browser with split-screen and online multiplayer.
  • How an online community took back the Legend of Zelda

The service is launching as a pilot program with gradually loosening physician oversight. entry.title: All the drama around AI’s takeover of mathematics

But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, […]
entry.content:
This past year, OpenAI, Anthropic, and other labs have announced breakthroughs on numerous long-standing mathematical problems, in some cases pushing well beyond what researchers expected current systems to be capable of — including resolving one of the famous Millennium Prize problems. But in classic Silicon Valley style, AI labs are moving fast and breaking things, barreling through the discipline with all the grace of a runaway bulldozer. Results that might normally have been celebrated have instead sparked backlash. AI labs say they are learning from earlier mistakes. Whether those promises bear fruit remains to be seen.
